taxonomy.subtopic: Platelet GPIb-mediated adhesion and stabilization of factor VIII

questions.stem_html: A 17-year-old girl has heavy menstrual bleeding, frequent epistaxis, and prolonged bleeding after dental extraction. Her platelet count is normal. A platelet-function screening test is prolonged, and activated partial thromboplastin time is mildly prolonged. The accompanying vessel-injury schematic shows a missing bridge between platelets and exposed subendothelial collagen. Deficiency of the same molecule also lowers the circulating concentration of which factor?
questions.explanation_html: Von Willebrand factor binds exposed subendothelial collagen and platelet glycoprotein Ib, supporting platelet adhesion under shear stress. It also binds and stabilizes factor VIII in plasma. Therefore, von Willebrand factor deficiency causes mucocutaneous bleeding from impaired primary hemostasis and may mildly prolong activated partial thromboplastin time because factor VIII is cleared more rapidly.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Factor V circulates independently and acts as a cofactor for factor Xa in the prothrombinase complex.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Factor VII initiates the extrinsic pathway after binding tissue factor and is not carried by von Willebrand factor.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Factor IX participates in the intrinsic tenase complex; its plasma stability does not depend on von Willebrand factor.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Factor XIII cross-links fibrin and is not stabilized by von Willebrand factor.

questions.educational_objective: Von Willebrand factor supports platelet adhesion through GPIb and stabilizes factor VIII; deficiency therefore impairs primary hemostasis and can reduce factor VIII activity.
